lessons.title: Five vowels inside consonant–vowel patterns
lessons.objective: Keep each Italian vowel pure inside ma me mi mo mu, then transfer the same movements into other consonant rows and real words.
lessons.explanation:
Keep each Italian vowel pure and clear inside ma me mi mo mu, with no glide at the end. Notice the tongue moving forward for mi and back with rounded lips for mu.
The m row
ma · me · mi · mo · mu
Close both lips for m, then open into the vowel. These are practice syllables, not five vocabulary words.
lips
Both lips meet
The tongue prepares for the next vowel; the lips make the closure.
Air passes through the nose during m.
Voice on
Say mmm → ma, then me, mi, mo, mu. Open from the same light lip closure each time.
Keep the nasal m audible before the vowel, and never let a vowel slide into a glide or an "uh".
lessons.speakingPrompt: In Italian, keep each Italian vowel pure inside ma me mi mo mu, then transfer the same movements into other consonant rows and real words. Use the scene: A map at home. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

items.note: MAP-pa: two pure a's, no "uh" at the end; hold the double p.
TA-vo-lo: stress on TA; every vowel stays pure, including the final o.
GUAR-da: gu + a is gwa; the final a stays open and never turns into "uh".
MO-to: pure open o with no "oh-oo" glide; the final o is fully sounded.
LU-na: u as in "moon" but shorter, with no y-glide and no "uh" ending.
CA-sa: single short s between vowels; both a's stay pure.

lessons.title: The m row
lessons.objective: Move through the five vowels without changing the m.
lessons.explanation:
Let the lips close lightly for m while the following vowel changes. Compare ma me mi mo mu without inserting a pause inside each unit; mattina starts with a clear m and a long tt.
The m row
ma · me · mi · mo · mu
Close both lips for m, then open into the vowel. These are practice syllables, not five vocabulary words.
lips
Both lips meet
The tongue prepares for the next vowel; the lips make the closure.
Air passes through the nose during m.
Voice on
Say mmm → ma, then me, mi, mo, mu. Open from the same light lip closure each time.
Keep the nasal m audible before the vowel.

items.note: mat-TI-na: light m, then hold the double t; the stressed i stays pure.
MA-no: light m, pure a and o, with no glide at the end.
va-LI-gia: gia is one syllable and the i is silent; stress on LI.
mo-NE-ta: stress on NE; every vowel clear and pure, final a included.
MU-si-ca: stress on the first syllable; c is a hard k before a.
cu-CI-na: ci is "chee"; stress on CI, with a hard c in the first syllable.

lessons.title: The p row
lessons.objective: Practise a brief, unaspirated p release without the strong puff of a stressed English p.
lessons.explanation:
Make a small lip closure and release into pa pe pi po pu. Keep the vowels pure and distinct with no English-style puff; the short form un po' (a little) uses the same light p.
The p row
pa · pe · pi · po · pu
Close both lips, release, then say the vowel. Italian p has almost no puff of air, unlike a stressed English p.
lips
Both lips meet, then release
The tongue prepares for the vowel. Keep the lip closure brief.
Briefly stop oral airflow, then release.
Voice off for the consonant
Say pa three times slowly, then pa → pi → pu, then pane → patata → porta. Feel the release with a hand in front of the mouth.
Use less aspiration than a strongly stressed English p; do not force a puff.
lessons.speakingPrompt: In Italian, practise a brief, unaspirated p release without the strong puff of a stressed English p. Use the scene: Buying fruit. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

items.note: pa-TA-ta: p with no puff of air; stress on the middle TA.
PA-ne: light p with no puff; pure a and a fully sounded final e.
pa-vi-MEN-to: unaspirated p; stress on MEN, and every vowel stays pure.
PO-co: p without a puff; open o, and a hard c before the final o.
PU-ro: pure u after a puffless p; one quick tap for the r.
POR-ta: unaspirated p, open o; the final a is not reduced.

lessons.title: The t row
lessons.objective: Find the Italian dental t placement at the back of the upper teeth.
lessons.explanation:
Touch the tongue tip lightly against the back of the upper front teeth for t. Practise ta te ti to tu, then return to normal stress in Teresa ha tempo per preparare il tè.
The t row
ta · te · ti · to · tu
Place the tongue tip against the back of the upper front teeth. Release into the vowel without a strong puff of air.
teeth
Tongue tip at the upper front teeth
Use a light contact on the back of the upper teeth, not the ridge behind them; release into the vowel.
Brief oral blockage, then release.
Voice off for the consonant
Say ta → ti → tu slowly. Notice the dental contact rather than an English-style ridge contact.
Avoid a strong puff or an extra vowel after t; never flap it.
lessons.speakingPrompt: In Italian, find the Italian dental t placement at the back of the upper teeth. Use the scene: Tea with Teresa. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

items.note: TAT-tsa: dental t with no puff; zz is a long ts.
TE: the grave accent marks the stressed final e; dental t, no puff.
TEM-po: tongue tip at the upper teeth, no puff; stress on TEM.
PREN-de: stress on PREN; the d uses the same dental place as t but is voiced.
TU-bo: dental t with no puff; pure u, and b closes both lips.
te-IE-ra: stress on IE; dental t, no puff, and the ie is one syllable.

lessons.title: The n and l rows
lessons.objective: Keep the consonant distinct while changing vowels, with a clear light l.
lessons.explanation:
Alternate na ne ni no nu and la le li lo lu. Keep nasal airflow for n and side airflow for l while the vowel changes; the Italian l stays clear in every position.
The n row
na · ne · ni · no · nu
Let air pass through the nose for n, then move into the vowel.
ridge
Tongue tip at the ridge behind the upper front teeth
Make a light closure; prepare the next vowel without pressing hard.
Air passes through the nose during n.
Voice on
Say nnn → na, then na → ni → nu. Release the tongue into each vowel.
Connected speech can move the contact place; that comes in the Core lessons.
The l row
la · le · li · lo · lu
Touch the ridge behind the upper teeth with the tongue tip; let air pass around the sides. The l is always clear.
ridge
Tongue tip near the ridge; sides leave space for airflow
Keep a light central tongue contact while air escapes at the sides; do not pull the tongue back.
Oral airflow around the sides of the tongue.
Voice on
Say la → li → lu, then luna → lampada → lettera. Notice the vowel change without losing the l.
Never use the dark English l of "full"; do not add an extra vowel before the l.
lessons.speakingPrompt: In Italian, keep the consonant distinct while changing vowels, with a clear light l. Use the scene: A note beside the lamp. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

items.note: LET-te-ra: clear light l, tongue tip up; hold the tt and tap the r once.
NU-vo-la: clear n and clear l; pure u, and stress on NU.
LAM-pa-da: stress on LAM; light l, never the dark English l.
LU-na: clear l and clear n; pure u, no "uh" at the end.
NOT-te: open o, clear n; hold the double t.
fi-NE-stra: stress on NE; clear n, and no vowel inside str.

lessons.title: The s and f rows
lessons.objective: Carry a continuous consonant into a steady vowel.
lessons.explanation:
Keep continuous airflow through sa se si so su and fa fe fi fo fu. Use the tongue groove for s and light lip-to-teeth narrowing for f.
The s row
sa · se · si · so · su
Make a continuous hiss, then move into the vowel. At the start of a word before a vowel the Italian s is always voiceless.
ridge
Tongue approaches the ridge; a narrow channel remains
Do not seal the mouth; form a groove and leave space for airflow.
Continuous oral airflow.
Voice off
Say sss → sa, then sa → si → su. Keep the beginning continuous, then say salotto → sedia.
This is a narrowing target, not a complete contact. Between vowels some speakers voice it; that comes in a later lesson.
The f row
fa · fe · fi · fo · fu
Rest the lower lip lightly against the upper front teeth and let air flow through the narrow gap.
lip-teeth
Upper front teeth near the lower lip
Leave a small opening instead of biting the lip.
Continuous oral airflow through the gap.
Voice off
Say fff → fa, then fa → fi → fu with a gentle, continuous beginning; then foto → famiglia → fratello.
Keep the lip contact light and the airflow steady.
lessons.speakingPrompt: In Italian, carry a continuous consonant into a steady vowel. Use the scene: Soup and a photograph. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

items.note: sa-LOT-to: the initial s is voiceless, a clean hiss; hold the tt.
mi-NE-stra: s before t stays a clean hiss; stress on NE.
SE-dia: two syllables, stress on SE; the initial s is voiceless.
FO-to: lower lip lightly on the upper teeth, steady f; open o.
fa-MI-glia: steady f; gli is one palatal l, and stress falls on MI.
fra-TEL-lo: f, then one quick tap r; hold the ll, stress on TEL.

lessons.title: One /k/ sound, two spellings
lessons.objective: Use one /k/ sound for c before a, o, u and ch before e, i, and keep it apart from qu.
lessons.explanation:
Use the tongue back for ka ke ki ko ku. Read the Italian spellings ca che chi co cu and keep sound cues separate from spelling; qu and cqu add a w, as in quindici and acqua.
The hard c row
ca · che · chi · co · cu
One sound, different spellings: c before a, o, u; ch before e, i. The h is silent; it only keeps the c hard.
velar
Back of tongue meets the soft palate, then releases
Keep the tongue tip relaxed while the tongue back closes and releases into the next vowel.
Brief oral blockage, then release.
Voice off for the consonant
Say ka → ki → ku → ke → ko slowly, then casa → chilo → culla. Start each vowel with a small tongue-back closure and release; avoid a large English-style puff.
Do not use the tongue tip for k. The h in che and chi is never pronounced; qu and cqu add a w (quindici, acqua).
lessons.speakingPrompt: In Italian, use one /k/ sound for c before a, o, u and ch before e, i, and keep it apart from qu. Use the scene: A small bar order. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

items.note: CA-sa: c is a hard k before a; no puff of air.
CHI-lo: ch is k before i; the h is only spelling.
QUIN-di-ci: qu is kw; stress on QUIN, and the final ci is "chee".
CA-li-ce: stress on CA; hard c before a, soft c ("ch") before e.
CUL-la: hard c before u; hold the double l.
AC-qua: cqu is a long kw; hold the k closure before the w.

lessons.title: One /g/ sound, two spellings
lessons.objective: Read hard g before all five vowels, with gh before e and i, and keep it apart from soft gi.
lessons.explanation:
Practise ga ghe ghi go gu after a pause. Hear the hard g in il gatto and keep it distinct from the soft gi in giardino; the h in ghe and ghi is only a spelling sign and is never sounded.
The hard g row
ga · ghe · ghi · go · gu
For this row, g before a, o, u and gh before e, i. The h is silent; it only keeps the g hard. Soft g (ge, gi) is a different sound.
velar
Back of tongue at the soft palate, closing and releasing
Start the row after a pause: the tongue back closes firmly, then releases into the vowel.
Brief oral blockage, then release.
Voice on
Say ga after a pause, then ga → ghe → ghi → go → gu, then gatto → funghi → gusto. Compare giardino, where gi is a soft sound.
The h in ghe and ghi is silent and adds no sound of its own. Gu + vowel (guida) sounds the u as w; gh never does.
lessons.speakingPrompt: In Italian, read hard g before all five vowels, with gh before e and i, and keep it apart from soft gi. Use the scene: A guitar in the garden. Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

items.note: GAT-to: voiced hard g; hold the double t.
FUN-ghi: gh keeps the g hard before i; the h is silent.
GOC-cia: hard g; cc before ia is a long "ch", with a silent i.
GU-sto: hard g before u; the u is fully sounded.
GUI-da: g, then a clear u glide into i (gwi); stress on GUI.
giar-DI-no: soft g, the "j" of jam; the i in gia is silent, stress on DI.

lessons.title: Gli, gn, and vowel review
lessons.objective: Build gli and gn as single palatal sounds from a model without splitting them into two.
lessons.explanation:
Practise glia glie gli glio gliu and gna gne gni gno gnu. Each is one palatal sound, slightly long between vowels; then review the five pure vowels in whole words.
The gli row
glia · glie · gli · glio · gliu
Say gli as one palatal sound, like the l in "million". It is not g followed by l.
palate
Tongue body flat against the hard palate
Press the middle of the tongue to the palate and let it slide away; keep the tongue tip down.
Air passes around the sides of the tongue.
Voice on
Say glia → glie → gli → glio → gliu, then figlio → bottiglia → famiglia. Hold it slightly long between vowels.
Do not say g + l, and do not add a separate i before the vowel in glia, glio, gliu.
The gn row
gna · gne · gni · gno · gnu
Say gn as one palatal nasal, like the ny in "canyon". It is not g followed by n.
palate
Tongue body flat against the hard palate
Press the middle of the tongue to the palate while air goes through the nose.
Air passes through the nose.
Voice on
Say gna → gne → gni → gno → gnu, then compagno → lavagna. Hold it slightly long between vowels.
Do not say g + n or n + y; gn is one sound. Plain n in domani is different.

Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

bot-TI-glia: gli is one palatal l, as in "million", never g + l.
com-PA-gno: gn like "canyon", one sound, slightly long.
la-VA-gna: gn like "canyon" in one sound; stress on VA.
do-MA-ni: stress on MA; this is plain n, not gn, so keep it short.
so-REL-la: one quick tap for the r; hold the double l.

lessons.title: Foundation transfer check
lessons.objective: Use unfamiliar words and a short passage after mixed sound rows.
lessons.explanation:
Mix the rows you have practised in words you have not drilled: pure vowels, unaspirated p, t and c, and hard versus soft c and g. Keep each sound clean when the word changes.
The hard c row
ca · che · chi · co · cu
One sound, different spellings: c before a, o, u; ch before e, i. The h only keeps the c hard and is never pronounced.
velar
Back of tongue meets the soft palate, then releases
Keep the tongue tip relaxed while the tongue back closes and releases into the next vowel.
Brief oral blockage, then release.
Voice off for the consonant
Say ca → che → chi → co → cu, then parco → pranzo → amico → ingresso. Keep the closure light and unaspirated.

lessons.title: B and v kept apart
lessons.objective: Keep b and v as two distinct sounds, never swapping one for the other.
lessons.explanation:
Contrast ba va be ve bo vo. In Italian b closes both lips and v is a lip-teeth friction sound, and the spelling always tells you which one to use.
B and v: two sounds
ba · va · be · ve · bo · vo
Italian keeps b and v apart. For b, both lips close; for v, the upper teeth touch the lower lip and air rubs through.
lips
b: both lips meet; v: upper teeth on the lower lip

b: brief stop, then release; v: continuous airflow through the gap.
Voice on for both

Never swap them: a b pronounced as v, or a v pronounced as b, changes the word.

lessons.title: Dental t and d
lessons.objective: Place both sounds at the upper teeth and compare voicing.
lessons.explanation:
Place the tongue tip at the upper teeth for both t and d; t is voiceless and d is voiced. Compare ta da te de ti di to do tu du, and keep the d from flapping between vowels.
The t row
ta · te · ti · to · tu
Place the tongue tip against the back of the upper front teeth. Release into the vowel without a strong puff of air; t is voiceless.
teeth
Tongue tip at the upper front teeth
Use a light contact on the back of the upper teeth, not the ridge behind them.
Brief oral blockage, then release.
Voice off for the consonant
Say ta → te → ti → to → tu, then tazza → tè → temperatura. Keep the contact at the teeth each time.
Avoid a strong puff or an extra vowel after t.
The d row
da · de · di · do · du
Use the same place as t, but with voice on. The d is a full stop, never a soft flap between vowels.
teeth
Tongue tip at the upper front teeth
Touch the back of the upper teeth with the same light contact as for t, then release into the vowel.
Brief oral blockage, then release.
Voice on
Say ta → da, te → de, ti → di, then dito → due → dove. Keep d as firm between vowels as at the start.
Do not soften or flap d between vowels, and do not use the English ridge contact.

lessons.title: Short and long consonants
lessons.objective: Hold double consonants about twice as long as single ones and shorten the vowel before them.
lessons.explanation:
A double consonant is held about twice as long as a single one, and the vowel before it is shorter. Compare casa and cassa, nono and nonno, sete and sette, fato and fatto.
Single and double consonants
ata · atta · ana · anna · asa · assa
Hold a double consonant about twice as long as a single one, and keep the vowel before it short. Double letters mean a longer sound, not two sounds.
timing
Same articulator, held longer
Close or narrow the same place, then wait before releasing; do not repeat the consonant twice.
The airflow is stopped or narrowed for about twice as long; nothing extra is added.
Voicing follows the letter: tt stays voiceless, nn stays voiced
Say ata → atta, ana → anna, asa → assa, then casa → cassa, sete → sette, nono → nonno.
Do not stress or repeat the first half; make one long closure and one release.

velar
Tongue back held against the soft palate
Close the tongue back firmly and hold the closure before the release.
Oral airflow stops for the whole hold.

ridge
One quick tongue-tip contact near the ridge

lessons.objective: Use hard and soft c correctly and map each sound to its spelling.
lessons.explanation:
Use cia ce ci cio ciu for soft c and contrast it with ca co cu. Before e and i, c sounds like ch; in cia, cio and ciu the i is only a spelling sign.
The soft c row
cia · ce · ci · cio · ciu
Close the tongue blade just behind the ridge and release it slowly into a hiss, as in 'chess'. Before e and i, the letter c always has this sound.
postalveolar
Tongue blade just behind the ridge; closure released into friction
Let the closure open into friction instead of a sharp release; round the lips slightly for cio and ciu.

Voice off

Open and closed e and o
é · è · ó · ò

lessons.title: When the u is heard
lessons.objective: Hear and say the u in gu and qu while keeping ch and gh free of it.

qua · que · qui · quo · cuo

velar
Back of the tongue at the soft palate, then lips rounding

lessons.objective: Learn the sounds of z and x and common place names without inventing a universal rule.

The z row
za · ze · zi · zo · zu

teeth

A brief closure, then friction.
Voice off for ts; voice on for dz

vowels

lessons.title: Pr and br clusters
lessons.objective: Keep each cluster together without adding an extra vowel.

The p row
pa · pe · pi · po · pu
Close both lips and release straight into a tap r: pra, pre, pri, pro, pru. No vowel comes between p and r.
lips
Both lips meet, then release
The tongue prepares for the vowel. Keep the lip closure brief and the release soft.
Briefly stop oral airflow, then release.
Voice off for the consonant

The b row
ba · be · bi · bo · bu
Close both lips fully for b, then release into one quick tap r: bra, bre, bri, bro, bru.
lips
Both lips close fully
Close the lips completely, then release into the vowel without letting air leak through.
Briefly stop oral airflow, then release.
Voice on

Do not leave the lips slightly open; b is a full closure and never a v.
The single r
ara · ere · iri · oro · uru

ridge
One quick tongue-tip tap near the ridge
Keep the gesture brief and loose, then return to the vowel.
A very brief interruption in oral airflow.
Voice on
Say ara → ere → oro, then prima → libro → braccio.
Use a vowel-r-vowel pattern for the tap; a word beginning with r takes the trill instead.

lessons.title: Tr and dr clusters
lessons.objective: Move from a dental closure into the tap r.
lessons.explanation:
Practise tra tre tri tro tru and dra dre dri dro dru with light contact. Follow the chosen speaker model; do not force an extra vowel between the consonants.
The t row
ta · te · ti · to · tu
Touch the back of the upper teeth for t, then tap r at once: tra, tre, tri, tro, tru.
teeth
Tongue tip at the back of the upper front teeth
Touch the back of the upper teeth lightly and release into the vowel without a puff.
Brief oral blockage, then release.
Voice off for the consonant
Say ta → ti → tu slowly, then treno → tre → pietra → entrata.
Avoid an English-style puff and do not touch the ridge; the contact is at the teeth.
The d row
da · de · di · do · du
Use the same teeth contact with voice for d, then tap r at once: dra, dre, dri, dro, dru.
teeth
Tongue tip at the back of the upper front teeth
Use the same place as t, with the voice on, then release into the vowel.
Brief oral blockage, then release.
Voice on
Say da → di → du, then madre → dritto.
Do not flap d between vowels; keep a clear closure at the teeth.
The single r
ara · ere · iri · oro · uru
Use one quick tip tap for the r straight after the dental: ara, ere, iri, oro, uru.
ridge
One quick tongue-tip tap near the ridge
Keep the gesture brief and loose, then return to the vowel.
A very brief interruption in oral airflow.
Voice on
Say ara → ere → oro, then treno → madre → dritto.
Use a vowel-r-vowel pattern for the tap; a word beginning with r takes the trill instead.

lessons.title: Cr and gr clusters
lessons.objective: Build a velar-to-r cluster in a real word.
lessons.explanation:
Practise cra cre cri cro cru and gra gre gri gro gru. Keep the cluster compact, then say a complete phrase with ordinary stress.
The hard c row
ca · che · chi · co · cu
Close the back of the tongue for c, then tap r with no vowel between: cra, cre, cri, cro, cru.
velar
Back of the tongue meets the soft palate
Keep the tongue tip relaxed while the back closes and releases; ch before e and i spells the same k.
Brief oral blockage, then release.
Voice off for the consonant
Say ca → chi → cu slowly, then crema → croce.
Avoid a strong puff; the h in che and chi is only a spelling sign.
The hard g row
ga · ghe · ghi · go · gu
Close the back of the tongue with voice for g, then tap r: gra, gre, gri, gro, gru.
velar
Back of the tongue meets the soft palate
Use the same closure as k, with the voice on; gh before e and i keeps g hard.
Brief oral blockage, then release.
Voice on
Say ga → ghi → gu slowly, then grande → gruppo → grazie.
Keep the g hard in gr, as in ga, go, gu, ghe and ghi; ge and gi spell a different, soft sound.
The single r
ara · ere · iri · oro · uru
Use one quick tip tap for the r straight after the velar: ara, ere, iri, oro, uru.
ridge
One quick tongue-tip tap near the ridge
Keep the gesture brief and loose, then return to the vowel.
A very brief interruption in oral airflow.
Voice on
Say ara → ere → oro, then crema → grande → grazie.
Use a vowel-r-vowel pattern for the tap; a word beginning with r takes the trill instead.

lessons.title: Clusters with l
lessons.objective: Keep pl, bl, fl, cl and gl as clusters.
lessons.explanation:
Practise pla ple pli plo plu, then switch to bla, fla, cla and gla with the same vowel order. Keep the l joined to the preceding consonant, and notice that Italian often has pi, bi and fi where you might expect pl, bl and fl: piatto, bianco, fiore.
The p row
pa · pe · pi · po · pu
Close both lips for p and go straight into a light l: pla, ple, pli, plo, plu.
lips
Both lips meet, then release
The tongue prepares for the vowel. Keep the lip closure brief and the release soft.
Briefly stop oral airflow, then release.
Voice off for the consonant
Say pa → pi → pu, then plastica.
Italian p has no puff of air; do not force an English-style aspirated p.
The b row
ba · be · bi · bo · bu
Close both lips with voice for b and go straight into a light l: bla, ble, bli, blo, blu.
lips
Both lips close fully
Close the lips completely, then release into the vowel without letting air leak through.
Briefly stop oral airflow, then release.
Voice on
Say ba → bu, then blu → blusa.
Do not leave the lips slightly open; b is a full closure and never a v.
The f row
fa · fe · fi · fo · fu
Make narrow friction for f and go straight into a light l: fla, fle, fli, flo, flu.
lip-teeth
Upper teeth touch the lower lip
Let a narrow stream of air pass between the upper teeth and the lower lip.
Continuous oral airflow with friction.
Voice off
Say fa → fi, then flauto → fiore, where Italian has fi instead of fl.
Do not close the lips completely; f is friction, not a lip closure.
The hard c row
ca · che · chi · co · cu
Close the back of the tongue for c and go straight into l: cla, cle, cli, clo, clu.
velar
Back of the tongue meets the soft palate
Keep the tongue tip relaxed while the back closes and releases; ch before e and i spells the same k.
Brief oral blockage, then release.
Voice off for the consonant
Say ca → cu, then classe → Clelia.
Avoid a strong puff; the h in che and chi is only a spelling sign.
The hard g row
ga · ghe · ghi · go · gu
Close the back of the tongue with voice for g and go straight into l: gla, gle, glo, glu.
velar
Back of the tongue meets the soft palate
Use the same closure as k, with the voice on; gh before e and i keeps g hard.
Brief oral blockage, then release.
Voice on
Say ga → gu, then globo → gloria.
Before i, gl usually spells the single palatal sound of figlio; in globo and gloria you hear a hard g followed by l.
The l row
la · le · li · lo · lu
Keep l light and clear after each consonant; the tongue tip rises quickly and the cluster stays tight.
ridge
Tongue tip at the ridge
Lift the tongue tip and let air pass along the sides; keep l clear, never dark as in English 'full'.
Oral airflow along the sides of the tongue.
Voice on
Say la → li → lu, then plastica → classe → globo → flauto.
Keep l light and clear in every position, including right after another consonant.

lessons.title: Finding syllables
lessons.objective: Use helpful syllable divisions in Italian without treating every letter as one beat.
lessons.explanation:
Use whole-word chunks: map-pa, cit-tà, scuo-la, sta-zio-ne. Keep the existing consonants and vowels; a double consonant splits across two syllables, and letters do not each receive a separate beat.
Syllables with double consonants
pal-la · tut-to · mam-ma · cit-tà · bot-te
Hold each double consonant across the syllable break: the first half closes the syllable and the second half starts the next. Say each word as one smooth chunk.
timing
Closure held about twice as long, split between two syllables
Close the syllable on the first half of the double consonant and release into the vowel only at the second half.
Air is stopped or narrowed for the whole hold, then released into the vowel.
Voicing stays the same as for the single consonant; only the length changes.
Say pal-la → tut-to → mam-ma slowly, then map-pa and cit-tà at normal speed without losing the hold.
Avoid inserting a vowel inside the double or shortening it to a single consonant.

Ask a follow-up question and close by confirming the meaning. Keep one sound target clear; a correct transcript is not proof of pronunciation.

cit-TÀ: hold the tt across the syllable break; stress falls on the final, accented a.
STRA-da: the s joins the next syllable; one quick tap r after the t.
sta-ZIO-ne: three syllables; z is ts, io glides, and the s joins the t.

lessons.title: Default word stress
lessons.objective: Use ordinary Italian stress patterns as a reading aid.
lessons.explanation:
Contrast the stress in CAR-ta and mes-SAG-gio inside whole words. Most Italian words stress the next-to-last syllable; many common words, such as TA-vo-lo, stress the third from last with no written mark.
The m row
ma · me · mi · mo · mu
Close both lips for m and release into a clear vowel; then keep the stressed syllable longer and the other syllables light but full.
lips
Both lips together, nasal
Close the lips lightly, lower the soft palate, and release into the vowel.
Air passes through the nose while the lips stay closed.
Voice on.
Say ma → mi → mu slowly, then TA-vo-lo, CAR-ta and mes-SAG-gio with the stress clear.
Avoid opening the lips early or adding a vowel after m.

items.note: TA-vo-lo: stress on the third syllable from the end; the last two vowels stay light but clear.
CAR-ta: stress on the next-to-last syllable, the most common pattern in Italian.
GIO-va-ne: stress on the first syllable; the i in gio is only a spelling sign.
o-ro-LO-gio: stress on LO; one single soft g, and the i in gio is silent.
mes-SAG-gio: hold ss and gg long; stress on SAG and the i is silent.
fra-TEL-lo: stress on TEL; hold the ll and tap the r once.

lessons.title: Written accents
lessons.objective: Use a written accent to locate final stress and notice the words that carry no mark.
lessons.explanation:
Let the written accent identify the stressed syllable in caffè, città and perché; then notice that medico, facile, numero and telefono carry no mark. Keep clear vowels in the unstressed syllables too.
The hard c row
ca · che · chi · co · cu
Start with ca che chi co cu: lift the back of the tongue to the soft palate and release cleanly, then say caffè with the stress on the final vowel.
velar
Back of the tongue against the soft palate
Raise the back of the tongue to the soft palate and release into the vowel without a puff.
Brief blockage at the back of the mouth, then a small release.
Voice off for the consonant.
Say ca → co → cu slowly, then caf-FÈ, ME-di-co and te-LE-fo-no with the stress clear.
Avoid a puff of air; in che and chi the silent h only keeps the c hard.

ta · te · ti · to · tu

teeth
Tongue tip against the back of the upper front teeth
Use a light dental contact and release straight into the vowel.
Brief oral blockage, then release with no strong puff.

lessons.objective: Match rhythm and intonation to a courteous request.

lips

lessons.title: Emotion without losing clarity
lessons.objective: Compare surprise, reassurance, and neutral delivery while keeping Italian vowels and doubles clear.
lessons.explanation:
Warm up with sa se si so su. Say the same phrase neutrally, with surprise (Davvero?) and with reassurance (Tranquillo, ce la facciamo), keeping every word, double consonant and final vowel intact.
The s row
sa · se · si · so · su
Make a steady s, then move into the vowel. At the start of a word before a vowel the s is voiceless, even when you sound surprised.
ridge
Tongue tip close to the ridge behind the upper teeth, with a narrow groove

Continuous airflow through the groove.
Voice off
Say sss → sa, then sa → so → sorpresa → Che sorpresa! Keep the start of the word continuous.

velar

lessons.objective: Use clear c, ch, z, and double-consonant habits in a passage not drilled beforehand.
lessons.explanation:
Use cia ce ci cio ciu, then read this new passage once for meaning and once for delivery. Pick one sound target and keep natural stress across the whole reading.
The soft c row
cia · ce · ci · cio · ciu
Press the blade of the tongue behind the ridge and release into a hiss, like "ch" in "chess". In cia, cio and ciu the i only softens the c.
postalveolar
Blade of the tongue just behind the ridge, lips slightly rounded
Release the closure into friction in one smooth movement; do not add an extra vowel.
A short stop followed by a hissing release.
Voice off
Say cia → cio → ciu, then ce → ci → cerca → Cerca una chiave.

lessons.objective: Retell a message while preserving meaning, clear stress, and pure vowels.
lessons.explanation:

lips
Both lips close and the soft palate lowers

Airflow through the nose.

lessons.objective: Stay clear when the listener needs precise names, numbers, and spelling.
lessons.explanation:
Use na ne ni no nu, then slow down only the information that needs precision. Say addresses in Italian order (via Roma 12, interno 3) and spell names with city names (A come Ancona).
The n row
na · ne · ni · no · nu
Touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind the upper teeth and let the air flow through the nose. Before c or g the n moves back (anche); before p or b it becomes m (un bacio).
ridge

Airflow through the nose.

ta · te · ti · to · tu
Touch the tongue tip to the back of the upper teeth, not the ridge, then release into the vowel with no puff of air.
teeth

lessons.explanation:

Airflow is interrupted for an instant.

lessons.objective: Speak clearly while explaining a routine problem to a colleague.
lessons.explanation:
Use pa pe pi po pu, then explain the work problem in clear meaning groups. Do not trade clarity for speed when you add a reason or a next step.
The p row
pa · pe · pi · po · pu
Close both lips, build a little pressure, and release into the vowel with no puff of air. Italian p is unaspirated, unlike English "pin".
lips
Both lips close completely

A brief release without a puff.
Voice off
Say pa → po → pu, then prova → passaggio → il passaggio non funziona.
The double pp (apparecchio) is held about twice as long as a single p, and p stays unaspirated at the start of a word too.

lessons.title: Regional doubling listening
lessons.objective: Recognize regional doubling across words while keeping one production model.
lessons.explanation:
Keep one consistent production model and recognize the other as a valid variant: the standard model doubles the next consonant after a, da, e, è, tre, più, chi (a casa, da me), while many northern speakers do not. Without real audio, treat this as a transcript and discussion task, not a listening test.
Doubling across words
a casa · da me · tre case · è vero · più forte
After a few short words the standard model lengthens the next consonant: a casa sounds like a-ccasa, da me like da-mme. Many northern speakers do not double, and that is a valid regional pattern.
timing
The first consonant of the next word is held a little longer
Say the two words as one rhythmic group and lengthen the first consonant of the second word.
Airflow follows the consonant you are holding.
Voicing follows the consonant being held
Say a casa → a-ccasa, da me → da-mme, then a voce → a-vvoce, tre chiavi → tre-cchiavi.
Speak with one model and recognize both when listening. Never call a regional pattern wrong, and do not double after words that do not trigger it.

lessons.title: Regional s and e/o listening
lessons.objective: Recognize regional s and open or closed e and o differences without mixing every feature.
lessons.explanation:
Compare the s between vowels (casa, rosa) only with identified speakers: it is voiced (ca-za) in much of the north and voiceless in the center and south, and neither is wrong. Open and closed e and o (as in perché or bene) also vary by region. Keep one production model and do not turn a regional difference into a rule for everyone.
Voiced and voiceless s
sole · sbaglio · casa · rosa · cosa
Say the s of sole voiceless and the s of sbaglio voiced like z. Between vowels (casa, rosa, cosa) northern speakers usually voice it and center-southern speakers usually do not.
ridge
Tongue tip close to the ridge, with a narrow groove
Keep the same groove for s and z; only the voice changes.
Continuous airflow through the groove.
Voice off in sole; voice on in sbaglio; regional between vowels
Say sole → sbaglio, then ca-sa → ca-za, then rosa → cosa → contesto.
Choose one model for speaking and recognize both when listening; the meaning does not change. The double ss (messaggio) is always voiceless and long.

lips

ra · re · ri · ro · ru
Let the tongue tip vibrate several times against the ridge, powered by the airflow rather than by muscle. At the start of a word the r is a short trill (risposta); rr is longer.
ridge

Push air steadily and let the tip flutter; do not tap once, and do not curl the tongue back.
Strong airflow that makes the tip vibrate.
